rules.title: Security Deposit Law - maximum deposit
rules.requirement: A landlord may not collect a security deposit of more than one and one-half times one month's rent, and any additional yearly deposit increase may not exceed 10% of the current deposit. Advance rents count toward the deposit, so the landlord may not require more than two and one-half times the monthly rent at the start of the lease, including the first month's rent.
rules.key_value: 1.5 times one month's rent; yearly increase no more than 10% of current deposit
rules.coverage_text: Most residential rental properties, including mobile homes, except owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, unless the tenant makes the law applicable 30 days after sending the landlord a written request to fulfill the Security Deposit Law's requirements.
rules.quoted_span: The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ).

rules.title: Security Deposit Law - deposit notice and interest
rules.requirement: Within 30 days of receiving the deposit and at each annual interest payment, the landlord must notify the tenant in writing of the bank or investment company holding the deposit, the deposit amount, the account type and the current interest rate. Interest belongs to the tenant.
rules.coverage_text: Most residential rental properties, including mobile homes, except owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, unless the tenant opts in by written request.
rules.penalty: If proper notice or interest is not given, the tenant may give written notice that the security money plus interest at 7% per annum be applied to rent; the landlord may not demand an additional security deposit.
rules.quoted_span: Within 30 days of receipt of the security deposit and at t he time of each annual interest payment, the landlord must notify the tenant in writing of the name and address of the banking institution or investment company in which the money is deposited, the amount of the deposit, type of account, and current rate o f interest for the account.

rules.title: Security Deposit Law - return of deposit
rules.requirement: Within 30 days after the tenancy ends, the landlord must return the security deposit plus interest less deductions, with an itemized list of any deductions sent by registered or certified mail.
rules.coverage_text: Most residential rental properties, including mobile homes, except owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, unless the tenant opts in by written request.
rules.penalty: The court may award the tenant double the amount wrongly withheld, together with court costs and reasonable attorney's fees.
rules.quoted_span: Within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy, a landlord must return the security deposit, plus interest earned less deductions, to the tenant ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.1).

rules.title: Security Deposit Law - return on displacement
rules.requirement: Within five business days after a tenant is displaced by fire, flood, condemnation or evacuation, the landlord must return the security deposit when a public official has posted a notice prohibiting occupancy or certified the displacement will last longer than seven days.
rules.coverage_text: Most residential rental properties, including mobile homes, except owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, unless the tenant opts in by written request.
rules.quoted_span: Within five (5) business days after a tenant is displaced by fire, flood, condemnation, or evacuation, the landlord must return the security deposit.

rules.title: New Jersey Law Against Discrimination - source of lawful income
rules.requirement: Landlords may not discriminate in renting housing and must give equal treatment regardless of protected characteristics, including source of lawful income.
rules.coverage_text: All landlord-tenant relationships, except two-family owner-occupied dwellings, rooms in an owner- or resident-occupied single home, and single-sex residences.
rules.exemptions: Two-family owner occupied dwellings, rooms in an owner or resident-occupied single home, and residences planned exclusively for and occupied by one sex; age-restricted housing as it pertains to familial status.
rules.penalty: Fines and penalties up to $10,000 for a first offense (N.J.S.A. 10:5-14.1a(a)); monetary damages and possible requirement to rent the unit to the complainant.
rules.quoted_span: The New Jersey Law Against Discrimination (LAD), N.J.S.A. 10:5-12(g) to -(h), prohibits discrimination when selling or renting property and requires equal treatment in the sale or rental of housing regardless of race, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, sex, marital status, civil union status, domestic partnership status, familial status, affectional or sexual orientation, gender  identity or expression, mental and physical disability, nationality, or source of lawful income.
